Sources & safety

Useful guidance, careful boundaries.

WagSignals is an educational starting point for noticing patterns in dog behavior—not a diagnosis, behavior assessment, or substitute for hands-on professional care.

A dog’s anatomy, health, history, and situation all change the meaning of a signal. When safety is uncertain, create space first.
Use it well

A few rules keep the read kind and useful.

Look at the whole dog, compare changes with their normal baseline, and leave room for the dog to choose. Do not deliberately provoke a dog to test a signal.

  • 01
    Whole dog, whole momentEyes, ears, mouth, posture, tail, movement, and context work together.
  • 02
    Health can change behaviorSudden, persistent, painful, or unusual changes deserve veterinary advice.
  • 03
    Warnings are informationDo not punish growling, freezing, or teeth displays. Stop pressure and add distance.
  • 04
    Children need active supervisionNever leave a young child and a dog together without an attentive adult.
  • 05
    Get help earlyBite risk, repeated aggression, guarding, panic, or unsafe handling need qualified support.
  • 06
    Choose humane trainingReward-based teaching keeps learning clear and protects trust.

Educational guidance, not a diagnosis. For repeated or high-risk concerns, contact a qualified reward-based professional or veterinarian.
